questions.stem: What does the phase of a wave determine?
choices: The maximum displacement of the wave
The time period of the wave
The displacement of the wave at any position and instant
The distance between two consecutive crests
questions.solution: The phase of a wave determines the displacement of the wave at any position and instant because it represents the state of the wave at a specific point in space and time. The maximum displacement is determined by the amplitude, the time period is related to the frequency, and the distance between two consecutive crests is the wavelength.

questions.stem: How does the crest of a wave progress with time?
choices: It remains stationary
It moves in the negative direction of x-axis
It moves in the positive direction of x-axis
It oscillates randomly
questions.solution: The crest of a wave progresses in the positive direction of the x-axis with time because the wave travels in that direction as time increases. This is consistent with the behavior of a traveling wave, where the position of the crest changes over time. The other options do not align with the fundamental properties of wave motion.

questions.stem: If a wave is propagating through a medium, what does the wavefront represent?
choices: The direction of the wave
The energy carried by the wave
The locus of points with the same phase
The frequency of the wave
questions.solution: A wavefront represents the set of points in a medium that are oscillating in the same phase at a given time. This is a fundamental property of waves, as it describes how the wave's motion spreads through space. The other options do not accurately describe what a wavefront represents.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be concluded about the propagation of waves in a medium?
choices: Only transverse waves can propagate in all media.
Only longitudinal waves can propagate in all media.
Both transverse and longitudinal waves can propagate in solids.
Only surface waves can propagate in liquids.
questions.solution: Solids have the necessary rigidity to support both transverse and longitudinal waves, as transverse waves involve particle motion perpendicular to the wave direction, and longitudinal waves involve particle motion parallel to the wave direction. Fluids lack the shear strength required for transverse waves, so only longitudinal waves can propagate through them. The other options are incorrect because not all media support only one type of wave, and surface waves are not the only type that can exist in liquids.

तरल में केवल सतही तरंगें ही प्रसारित हो सकती हैं।
hi.solution: ठोस में आवश्यक कठोरता होती है जो अनुप्रस्थ और अनुदैर्ध्य दोनों प्रकार की तरंगों को समर्थित करती है, क्योंकि अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों में कण के गति तरंग दिशा के लंबवत होती है और अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगों में कण के गति तरंग दिशा के समांतर होती है। द्रव्य में अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों के लिए आवश्यक कर्षण क्षमता नहीं होती, इसलिए केवल अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें इनमें प्रसारित हो सकती हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि सभी माध्यम एक प्रकार की तरंग को ही समर्थित नहीं करते हैं और तरल में केवल सतही तरंगें ही अस्तित्व में हो सकती हैं।
